info.title: Recoup API - Research
info.description: API documentation for the Recoup platform - an AI agent platform for the music industry

get.description: Returns chats for the authenticated account. Personal Bearer tokens see only the caller's chats; org keys see chats across the org's member accounts; admin keys see all chats. Each row carries the chat id and the session id needed to build the chat URL.

post.description: Generate AI-powered text responses using the Recoup chat system. This endpoint processes chat requests and returns generated text along with metadata about the generation process.

Stream AI-powered chat responses using the Recoup chat system. This endpoint mirrors the request payload of the Chat Generate API but returns a streaming response compatible with the Vercel AI SDK `createUIMessageStreamResponse`. The stream emits UI message parts encoded as data chunks that can be parsed with `createUIMessageStreamParser`.

200.description: Streaming response with UI message parts. Events include: message-start (assistant begins message), message-delta (incremental updates), message-end (assistant finishes message), error (stream error), and metadata (usage data).

schema.description: Server-Sent Events stream containing UI message parts

post.description: Streams an agent loop running as a durable [Vercel Workflow](https://vercel.com/docs/workflow) against the session's sandbox. The agent uses sandbox-only tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `grep`, `glob`, `todo`, `task`, `ask_user_question`, `skill`, `fetch`) — no MCP or Composio. Requires a sandbox provisioned via [POST /api/sandbox](/api-reference/sandbox/create). Parallel to [POST /api/chat](/api-reference/chat/stream) — does not replace it.

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream of UI message parts compatible with the Vercel AI SDK `createUIMessageStreamResponse`. The `x-workflow-run-id` response header carries the durable workflow run ID for resume/stop operations.

x-workflow-run-id.description: Durable workflow run ID. Persist alongside the chat so a later `GET /api/chat/{chatId}/stream` request can resume this run after a disconnect.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events stream containing UI message parts

409.description: Another workflow is already running for this chat and could not be resumed.

get.description:
Unified Chartmetric search. This is the discovery primitive for the detail-lookup endpoints — use `type=artists` to find an `id` for [GET /api/research/albums](/api-reference/research/albums), `type=tracks` for [GET /api/research/track](/api-reference/research/track), `type=playlists` for [GET /api/research/playlist](/api-reference/research/playlist), etc. Pick the right `id` from the returned results and pass it to the appropriate detail endpoint.

Thin proxy over Chartmetric's `/search`. Chartmetric's default search engine is narrow — for ambiguous queries like `Hotline Bling` or `Flowers` it often returns a single low-quality match. **Pass `beta=true` for higher relevance and accuracy**, which switches Chartmetric to its improved ranking engine. Beta results include a numeric `match_strength` score and have a slightly different shape than the default engine (see the response schema).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search query. Can be a name (e.g. `Drake`, `Flowers`) or a streaming-platform URL (e.g. `https://open.spotify.com/artist/...`).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Entity type to search.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results.

parameters.name: beta
parameters.description: When `true`, switches Chartmetric to its improved beta search engine — recommended for ambiguous queries. Results come back sorted by `match_strength` (higher is better) and include `target`/`platform` fields instead of the default-mode shape.

parameters.name: platforms
parameters.description: Comma-separated platforms to include in beta results (e.g. `cm,spotify`). Only valid with `beta=true`; ignored otherwise.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Pagination offset. Defaults to 0 when omitted.

400.description: Validation error (e.g., missing required query parameter `q`)

401.description: Authentication failed — invalid or missing API key

get.description:
Get the album discography — albums, EPs, and singles with release dates — for a Chartmetric `artist_id`.

Thin proxy over Chartmetric's `/artist/:id/albums`. By default `is_primary=true`, so only albums where the artist is a main artist are returned — DJ compilations, soundtracks, and pure feature appearances are excluded. Pass `is_primary=false` to include them. Discover a Chartmetric `artist_id` via [GET /api/research](/api-reference/research/search) with `type=artists&beta=true`.

parameters.name: artist_id
parameters.description: Chartmetric artist ID (positive integer). Obtain via [GET /api/research](/api-reference/research/search) with `type=artists&beta=true` — the `id` field in each result is the Chartmetric ID to pass here.

parameters.name: is_primary
parameters.description: When `true` (default), returns only albums where the artist is a main artist. Set to `false` to include feature appearances, DJ compilations, and soundtracks.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of albums to return. Defaults to Chartmetric's default (100) when omitted.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Pagination offset. Defaults to 0 when omitted.

400.description: Validation error — `artist_id` missing or not a positive integer

401.description: Authentication failed — invalid or missing API key

get.description:
Get full Chartmetric track metadata by numeric track `id` — title, artists, albums, release date, genres, popularity, and platform IDs.

This endpoint is a thin proxy over Chartmetric's `/track/:id` detail lookup. Discover a Chartmetric track ID via [GET /api/research](/api-reference/research/search) with `type=tracks&beta=true` — pick a result's `id`, then call this endpoint. Keeping the two concerns separate means predictable credit charging and no silent wrong-match behavior for ambiguous queries.

get.description:
Returns playlists featuring a specific track. Accepts a Chartmetric track ID (`id`) or a track name + optional artist (`q`, `artist`) for a Spotify-powered lookup. When no filter flag is passed, defaults to editorial + indie + majorCurator + popularIndie = `true`. Costs 5 credits per request.

Discover a Chartmetric track `id` via [GET /api/research](/api-reference/research/search) with `type=tracks&beta=true` — then pass the resulting `id` here for the most reliable match (avoids the ambiguity of name-based lookup).

parameters.name: id

ResearchAudienceResponse.description: Audience demographics and engagement metrics from Chartmetric. Contains two parallel families of fields: **followers** (`audience_*` and `top_*`) describe the artist's follower base, while **likers** (`audience_likers_*`, `likers_top_*`) describe the people who engage (like/comment) with the artist's posts. Engagement aggregates (`followers`, `avg_likes_per_post`, `engagement_rate`) and `notable_followers` round out the payload. All array shapes are upstream Chartmetric objects that pass through via `additionalProperties`.

timestp.description: ISO timestamp at which this audience snapshot was captured.

followers.description: Follower count on the underlying platform at snapshot time.

avg_commments_per_post.description: Note: field name is misspelled upstream as `avg_commments_per_post`.

likers_top_countries.description: Top countries for the likers (engagement) cohort.

likers_top_cities.description: Top cities for the likers cohort.

audience_genders.description: Gender breakdown of the follower base.

audience_genders_per_age.description: Follower gender split per age bracket.

audience_brand_affinities.description: Brand affinity scores for the follower cohort.

audience_likers_brand_affinities.description: Brand affinity scores for the likers cohort.

notable_followers.description: Notable public/influential accounts in the follower base.

ResearchCareerResponse.description: Career timeline — milestones, trajectory, and career stage history.

data.description: Chart entries for the requested platform/type/country/interval combination. Entry shape varies by platform; common fields include track/artist names, ranks, and platform-specific metrics.

ResearchCuratorResponse.description: Curator profile. Follower counts are split by platform (`instagram_followers`, `facebook_followers`, `twitter_followers`, `youtube_subscribers`, `soundcloud_followers`, `tiktok_followers`), each nullable when unknown. Aggregated signals live under `cm_statistics`.

user_id.description: Platform-native curator/user ID (e.g. Spotify user ID).

last_updated.description: ISO timestamp of the last Chartmetric sync.

suspicion_score.description: Chartmetric's internal suspicion score (lower is better).

spotifySocialUrls.description: Spotify-linked social URLs for the curator.

cm_statistics.description: Aggregated Chartmetric statistics — playlist reach, editorial counts, velocity deltas, etc.

ResearchDeepRequest.description: Request body for deep research. Performs comprehensive multi-source analysis.

query.description: The research question — be specific and detailed for best results.

content.description: The full research report as markdown.

citations.description: Source URLs cited in the report.

input.description: What to research (e.g., "Drake rapper from Dallas Texas").

schema.description: JSON schema defining the fields to extract. Must include `"type": "object"` at the top level.

output.description: Structured data matching the provided schema.

citations.description: Source citations supporting the enriched output.

field.description: Which output field this citation supports.

objective.description: What information to focus on (optional, max 3000 chars).

full_content.description: Return full page content instead of focused excerpts.

errors.description: URLs that failed to extract. Only present when one or more URLs could not be processed.

ResearchInstagramPostsResponse.description: Top Instagram posts and reels sorted by engagement. Fields are returned directly from Chartmetric's DeepSocial integration.

ResearchLookupResponse.description: Artist profile resolved from a platform URL or ID. Cross-platform IDs are nested inside a `data` object.

data.description: Cross-platform artist identifiers returned by Chartmetric.

ResearchMetricsResponse.description:
Time-series metrics for the artist on the selected platform. Shape varies by platform — fields at the root (not wrapped in a `data` envelope) each hold their own time-series array of `{timestp, value}` points.

For Spotify, expect `followers`, `listeners`, `popularity`, and `followers_to_listeners_ratio`. Other platforms expose their own set (e.g. `subscribers` and `views` for `youtube_channel`).

link.description: Canonical source URL on the upstream platform (e.g. the artist's Spotify URL).

followers.description: Time series of follower counts, when applicable to the source.

listeners.description: Time series of listener counts (e.g. Spotify monthly listeners), when applicable.

popularity.description: Time series of the platform's popularity score, when applicable.

followers_to_listeners_ratio.description: Derived time series, when both followers and listeners are available (Spotify).

platform.description: Platform where the event occurred (e.g. spotify, apple_music).

track_name.description: Name of the track involved, if any.

query.description: Natural language search for people (e.g., "A&R reps at Atlantic Records").

id.description: Unique result identifier from the search provider.

publishedDate.description: Date the profile or page was published.

author.description: Author of the page, if available.

removed_at.description: When the track was removed (past placements only).

ResearchPlaylistResponse.description: Playlist metadata — name, description, follower count, track count, curator info, and Chartmetric-derived signals (editorial flag, suspicion score, active-ratio, week/month delta, mood/activity/genre tags).

id.description: Chartmetric playlist ID (same as the `id` query param).

owner_name.description: Curator display name (what used to be advertised as `curator_name`).

num_track.description: Track count on the playlist (note: field is `num_track`, not `num_tracks`).

editorial.description: True if this is a first-party editorial playlist (e.g. Spotify's RapCaviar).

code2.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code associated with the playlist, when known.

active_ratio.description: Fraction of days recently that the playlist was updated (Chartmetric-internal).

suspicion_score.description: Chartmetric's internal playlist-suspicion score (lower is better).

fdiff_week.description: Follower change over the last week.

fdiff_month.description: Follower change over the last month.

last_updated.description: ISO timestamp the playlist was last modified upstream.

sys_last_updated.description: ISO timestamp Chartmetric last synced the playlist.

ResearchProfileResponse.description: Full artist profile — identity, biography, genres, geography, label/management, and Chartmetric-derived ranks/statistics. For longitudinal platform metrics (Spotify followers/listeners over time, social stats, etc.) call `GET /api/research/metrics` instead.

code2.description: ISO country code associated with the artist.

band.description: True if the artist is a band/group rather than a solo act.

cm_artist_rank.description: Overall Chartmetric artist rank (lower is better).

cm_statistics.description: Aggregated cross-platform snapshot — Spotify followers/monthly_listeners, Instagram/TikTok/YouTube counts, chart positions, etc. Fields may be null per-platform.

genres.description: Primary/secondary/sub-genre breakdown. Object with keyed subgroups, not a flat array.

results.description: Matching artists with IDs, names, and basic metadata.

ResearchSearchResult.description:
Shape varies by `type` and search engine. Common fields are listed here; `additionalProperties: true` lets engine-specific fields pass through.

**Default engine (`beta=false`):** entries include `name`, `id`, `image_url`, plus type-specific fields like `artist_names[]` (tracks), `isrc` (tracks), `sp_followers`/`sp_monthly_listeners`/`cm_artist_score` (artists), `owner_name` (playlists), etc.

**Beta engine (`beta=true`):** entries include `name`, `id`, `imageUrl`, `target` (the entity type — e.g. `track`, `artist`, `playlist`), `platform` (e.g. `cm`, `spotify`), and `match_strength` (numeric relevance score, higher is better).

id.description: Chartmetric internal ID for use with the detail-lookup endpoints (`/api/research/track`, `/api/research/playlist`, `/api/research/albums`, etc.). Usually an integer; some playlist sources return a string.

image_url.description: Default-engine image URL. (Beta engine returns `imageUrl` instead.)

imageUrl.description: Beta-engine image URL. (Default engine returns `image_url` instead.)

match_strength.description: Beta-only relevance score — sort entries by this descending. Not present in default-engine results.

target.description: Beta-only entity type (`track`, `artist`, `playlist`, etc.). Not present in default-engine results.

platform.description: Beta-only source platform (e.g. `cm`, `spotify`). Not present in default-engine results.

career_stage.description: undiscovered, developing, mid-level, mainstream, superstar, or legendary.

recent_momentum.description: decline, gradual decline, steady, growth, or explosive growth.

ResearchTrackResponse.description: Track metadata — title, artists, albums, release date, genres, popularity, and platform IDs. Only the most commonly-used fields are enumerated here; the upstream Chartmetric response includes additional fields (e.g. `cm_statistics`, `activities`, `moods`) that pass through under `additionalProperties`.

artists.description: Credited artists. Each entry is a Chartmetric artist object; at minimum `id` and `name` are populated.

cm_statistics.description: Chartmetric's aggregated cross-platform statistics for the track — Spotify popularity/streams, TikTok video counts, YouTube views, Shazam counts, Apple/Deezer/Amazon playlist reach, weekly deltas, etc. Fields are often null for less-popular tracks. Opaque object; inspect an actual response for the full field set.

tempo.description: Track tempo in BPM, when available.

city_name.description: City where the venue is located.

events.description: Events the artist performed at this venue.

query.description: The search query — what you want to find on the web.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return.

country.description: ISO country code for regional results (e.g., 'US', 'GB').

ResearchWebResponse.description: Web search results with titles, URLs, and content snippets.

snippet.description: Content snippet from the search result.

formatted.description: Results formatted as markdown for easy reading.

UIMessage.description: A message in the chat conversation. See https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-core/ui-message for details.

role.description: The role of the message sender

content.description: The text content of the message

message.description: Error message describing what went wrong

chatId.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the chat room to update

topic.description: The new display name for the chat room. Must be between 3 and 50 characters.

ResearchErrorResponse.description: Error response returned by all research endpoints for validation failures (400) and authentication errors (401).

error.description: Human-readable error message describing what went wrong.
